title: Revise parallel-jobs design to answer review findings F1-F8
summary: Rewrite docs/design/parallel-jobs.md to answer review 1 (F1-F8). It builds on native PR landing (one PR per job, squash, local branch rebuilt after each landing), recommends one process per job over shared threads, and adds a shared-append-only-files section. The change is design only; no code.

defaults_applied.how: The change revises a design document in response to review, and the build stays a later job.
Claims cite the source files and lines read; numbers are labeled as estimates.
One focused edit to one design document.
The document is written for an outside reader, with the review findings summarized in it.
Collisions on shared files are handled by a rule on who writes them, not by a fix for one instance.
The review and the native PR landing design supply the missing detail.

assumptions: The review file's line numbers may have drifted after native PR landing shipped, so the producer re-reads the cited source before correcting them.
docs/design/native-pr-landing.md describes the shipped mechanism, and the revision follows it rather than redesigning it.
The design stays at 'proposed, review pending', ready for a second review; the revision does not mark itself accepted.
The roadmap and CHANGELOG are changed only if the repository's convention requires it for a design-only revision.

acceptance_criteria.text: F1: the design drops the claim that disjoint change jobs land through local replay. It states that each job lands through its own pull request by squash, and that Athena rebuilds the local branch on the merged commit after each landing. It cites docs/design/native-pr-landing.md. It says what happens to a job whose base is behind the new HEAD, and §7, the open question on plan, and the build order (§10) are rewritten to match.

F2: the design recommends one child process per job as the default. It lists why threads are not chosen (AgentDriver and Ui have no Send/Sync bound, a caught panic is not enough isolation) and says what a spike would have to show to restore threads. The process model covers how the launcher spawns workers, collects results and exit codes, and handles the kill switch.

F3: a section on shared append-only files (CHANGELOG.md, docs/decisions.md numbering, README.md) states concrete rules. These cover which job writes them, how number allocation avoids two jobs taking the same number, how the pool serializes jobs that name the same file, and what a collision test must check. It says which of these the landing check enforces and which are only hints.

F4-F8 are each answered. Duplicate job refs are rejected up front after resolving to ids. The kill-switch check comes before the job lock. The design prints the worst-case spend (N times the per-job cap) at the start of a run. Line references are corrected (run.rs 698, land_or_block 1165-1307, retry_landing 1424-1433), or the design says how the references now stand after native PR landing. The seven open questions are settled or carried forward with a stated decision.

The design status line and any review-response table map every finding F1-F8 to the section that answers it. Claims cite their sources, and numbers are labeled as estimates. The only files changed are docs, with no source code or governance files.
Run `git diff --stat` and `git status`: only Markdown files under docs/ (and optionally CHANGELOG.md) changed. Run `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo test`: both still pass.

out_of_scope: Any code, tests, or build of the parallel-jobs feature
Changing native-pr-landing.md or the review file
Running the spike on thread safety
Editing governance files, records/, or athena.toml
